subject: Spanska 3
title: Expressing opinions: argumentation in Spanish
sourceSummary: Words and phrases for giving, agreeing with, and justifying an opinion: creo que, en mi opinión, estoy de acuerdo/en desacuerdo.

questions.opener: One of the most common ways to open an opinion.
questions.explanation: "Creo que" means "I think that" and is one of the most common ways to introduce an opinion, along with "pienso que".

questions.opener: A direct match for a phrase you already recognize.
questions.explanation: "En mi opinión" literally means "in my opinion" — a common phrase for introducing a personal stance.

questions.opener: The difference is a small prefix: en- or none at all.
questions.explanation: "Estoy de acuerdo" means "I agree". The opposite is "estoy en desacuerdo" or "no estoy de acuerdo" (I disagree).

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: "No creo que esto ___ (ser) una buena idea."
questions.opener: When you negate an opinion (no creo que...), the subjunctive is required in the clause — unlike the affirmative "creo que", which takes the indicative.
questions.explanation: "No creo que" negates the certainty of the statement and therefore triggers the subjunctive: "sea". Compare this with the affirmative form "creo que esto ES una buena idea", which takes the indicative because it expresses conviction, not doubt.

questions.prompt: Which word is used to JUSTIFY an opinion?
questions.explanation: "Ya que" means "since/because" and is used to justify a statement: "Creo que deberíamos reciclar más, ya que es bueno para el planeta." "Sin embargo" (however), "por otro lado" (on the other hand) and "aunque" (although) instead signal contrast.

questions.opener: Check the word order carefully — "que" should come right after the opinion expression, and "estar de acuerdo" needs a preposition to link to a statement.
choices: En mi opinión, que el examen fue difícil.
Creo que el examen fue difícil.
Creo el examen que fue difícil.
Estoy de acuerdo el examen fue difícil.
questions.explanation: "Creo que el examen fue difícil" has the correct structure: opinion expression + que + statement. "En mi opinión" doesn't take "que" (it isn't a verb), and "estoy de acuerdo" needs "con" or "en que" to link to a full clause: "estoy de acuerdo en que...".

questions.prompt: Find and correct the two errors: "En mi opinión, el uso de los móviles en la escuela son un problema serio, porque los estudiantes no presta atención en la clase."
questions.opener: Both errors involve the verb agreeing with the wrong word in the sentence.
questions.answer: En mi opinión, el uso de los móviles en la escuela es un problema serio, porque los estudiantes no prestan atención en la clase.
steps: "El uso ... son" has the wrong agreement — the subject is "el uso" (the use, singular), not "los móviles", so the verb should be singular: "es".
"Los estudiantes no presta" also has the wrong agreement — the subject "los estudiantes" is plural, so the verb should be "prestan".
The full corrected sentence: "En mi opinión, el uso de los móviles en la escuela es un problema serio, porque los estudiantes no prestan atención en la clase."
Tip: in long sentences with subordinate clauses, it's easy to let the verb agree with the wrong noun — always check which word is actually the subject.

questions.prompt: What phrases do you need to give, agree with, and justify an opinion?
questions.opener: A vocabulary list for argumentation, organized by function.
questions.answer: Give an opinion: creo que, pienso que, en mi opinión, a mi parecer, me parece que. Agree/disagree: estoy de acuerdo (con)/estoy en desacuerdo (con), no estoy de acuerdo. Justify: porque, ya que, puesto que (since/because), por eso (therefore). Contrast: sin embargo (however), por otro lado (on the other hand), aunque (although). Remember: "no creo que" and "dudo que" (I doubt that) take the subjunctive in the clause because they express doubt, while "creo que" and "pienso que" in affirmative form take the indicative.
